package @package@

import (
 "fmt"
 "math"
 "regexp"
 "strings"
 "sync"
)

// File retains logical paths and exact source bytes. Dependencies are not
// checkable inputs. OSG deliberately supplies its libraries as ordinary files.
type File struct { Filename, Raw string }
type Issue struct {
 Filename, Key, Severity, Message string
 Row, Column, EndRow, EndColumn int32
}
type Stats struct {
 Updates, Noops, IndexedObjects, ReaderVisits, DirtiedObjects, ParseRuns, ParseObjects int32
}

// Generated core globals assume sequential execution, including across Checkers.
var libraryMu sync.Mutex
var libraryWords = regexp.MustCompile(`(/[A-Z0-9_]{1,10}/)?[A-Z0-9_]{1,40}`)

// Checker owns a persistent registry. Failures panic with a cause: the host must
// refuse that check. Failed Prime/Update requires re-prime; a failed Check can
// be retried after the host restores an overlay with Update.
type Checker struct {
 registry @Registry@
 readers map[string]map[@Object@]bool
 words map[@Object@][]string
 stats Stats
}

// Prime replaces the baseline, including files, dependencies and config.
func (c *Checker) Prime(files, deps []File, config string) {
 libraryMu.Lock(); defer libraryMu.Unlock()
 *c = Checker{readers: map[string]map[@Object@]bool{}, words: map[@Object@][]string{}}
 h := @newRun@()
 for _, f := range files { h.@addFile@(str(f.Filename), str(f.Raw)) }
 for _, f := range deps { h.@addDependency@(str(f.Filename), str(f.Raw)) }
 c.registry = h.@parse@(str(config))
 // Iterate owners once. Looking up every filename here would scan the
 // entire registry twice per input and make priming quadratic.
 objects := c.registry.@getObjects@()
 defer objects.@close@()
 for {
  next := objects.@next@()
  if next.@done@ { break }
  c.index(next.@value@)
 }
}

func (c *Checker) require() {
 if c.registry == nil { panic("prime must succeed before check/update") }
}

func (c *Checker) index(obj @Object@) {
 c.stats.IndexedObjects++
 seen := map[string]bool{}
 files := obj.@getFiles@()
 for i := int32(0); i < libraryLength(files); i++ {
  file := any(libraryAt(files, i)).(@File@)
  for _, word := range libraryWords.FindAllString(strings.ToUpper(file.@getRaw@().String()), -1) { seen[word] = true }
 }
 c.words[obj] = make([]string, 0, len(seen))
 for word := range seen {
  if c.readers[word] == nil { c.readers[word] = map[@Object@]bool{} }
  c.readers[word][obj] = true
  c.words[obj] = append(c.words[obj], word)
 }
}
func (c *Checker) unindex(obj @Object@) {
 for _, word := range c.words[obj] {
  delete(c.readers[word], obj)
  if len(c.readers[word]) == 0 { delete(c.readers, word) }
 }
 delete(c.words, obj)
}

// Update batches edits without parsing. nil removes a file; &"" installs an
// empty file. The host implements overlay+restore by deferring Update(original).
// Lexical readers include comments/strings, matching OSG's conservative closure.
func (c *Checker) Update(filename string, raw *string) {
 libraryMu.Lock(); defer libraryMu.Unlock()
 c.require()
 c.stats.Updates++
 before := c.registry.@getFileByName@(str(filename))
 if raw == nil && before == nil || raw != nil && before != nil && before.@getRaw@().String() == *raw { c.stats.Noops++; return }
 var old @Object@
 if before != nil { old = c.registry.@findObjectForFile@(before) }
 if old != nil { c.unindex(old) }
 file := before
 var obj @Object@
 if raw == nil {
  c.registry.@removeFile@(before)
  if old != nil && libraryLength(old.@getFiles@()) > 0 { obj = old }
 } else {
  file = @newFile@(str(filename), str(*raw))
  if before == nil { c.registry.@addFile@(file) } else { c.registry.@updateFile@(file) }
  obj = c.registry.@findObjectForFile@(file)
 }
 dirty := map[@Object@]bool{}
 if obj != nil { c.index(obj); dirty[obj] = true }
 queue := []string{strings.ToUpper(file.@getObjectName@().String())}
 reached := map[string]bool{queue[0]: true}
 for at := 0; at < len(queue); at++ {
  for reader := range c.readers[queue[at]] {
   c.stats.ReaderVisits++
   if dirty[reader] { continue }
   dirty[reader] = true
   reader.@setDirty@()
   name := strings.ToUpper(reader.@getName@().String())
   if !reached[name] { reached[name] = true; queue = append(queue, name) }
  }
 }
 c.stats.DirtiedObjects += int32(len(dirty))
}

// Full-core arrays can be live views; small emitted packages use plain Items.
func libraryLength[T any](values *array[T]) int32 {
 if live, ok := any(values).(interface{ liveLength() int32 }); ok { return live.liveLength() }
 return int32(len(values.Items))
}
func libraryAt[T any](values *array[T], at int32) T {
 value := values.get(at)
 if !value.Has { panic("unexpected hole in core result array") }
 return value.Value
}

func libraryCoordinate(value any) int32 {
 var n float64
 switch v := value.(type) {
 case float64: n = v
 case int64: n = float64(v)
 case int32: n = float64(v)
 case optional[float64]: if !v.Has { panic("issue coordinate is undefined") }; n = v.Value
 case optional[int64]: if !v.Has { panic("issue coordinate is undefined") }; n = float64(v.Value)
 case optional[int32]: if !v.Has { panic("issue coordinate is undefined") }; n = float64(v.Value)
 default: panic(fmt.Sprintf("unsupported issue coordinate %T", value))
 }
 if math.IsNaN(n) || math.IsInf(n, 0) || math.Trunc(n) != n || n < math.MinInt32 || n > math.MaxInt32 { panic("issue coordinate is not a finite int32") }
 return int32(n)
}

// Check parses dirty objects lazily and runs rules for the file's owning object.
// Issue order/duplicates and coordinates are preserved; no CLI dump is parsed.
func (c *Checker) Check(filename string) []Issue {
 libraryMu.Lock(); defer libraryMu.Unlock()
 c.require()
 file := c.registry.@getFileByName@(str(filename))
 if file == nil { panic("file is not in the registry: " + filename) }
 obj := c.registry.@findObjectForFile@(file)
 if obj == nil { panic("object is not in the registry: " + filename) }
 dirty := int32(0)
 for object := range c.words { if object.@isDirty@() { dirty++ } }
 if dirty > 0 { c.stats.ParseRuns++; c.stats.ParseObjects += dirty }
 issues := c.registry.@findIssuesObject@(obj)
 out := make([]Issue, 0, libraryLength(issues))
 for at := int32(0); at < libraryLength(issues); at++ {
  issue := any(libraryAt(issues, at)).(@Issue@)
  start, end := issue.@getStart@(), issue.@getEnd@()
  out = append(out, Issue{Filename: issue.@getFilename@().String(), Key: issue.@getKey@().String(), Severity: issue.@getSeverity@().String(), Message: issue.@getMessage@().String(),
   Row: libraryCoordinate(start.@getRow@()), Column: libraryCoordinate(start.@getCol@()), EndRow: libraryCoordinate(end.@getRow@()), EndColumn: libraryCoordinate(end.@getCol@())})
 }
 return out
}
func (c *Checker) Stats() Stats { libraryMu.Lock(); defer libraryMu.Unlock(); return c.stats }
